Hex strings of H3 cells

Source: R/h3-type.R
rcs_h3_hex.Rd

Converts any vector of H3 cells to the 15-character lower-case hex strings that other H3 tools use. Inside a DuckDB connection prepared by the package, the SQL macro of the same name gives the same strings, so dplyr::mutate(cell = rcs_h3_hex(h3)) reads the same in both engines.

Usage

rcs_h3_hex(x)

Arguments

x

Cells: rcs_h3, bit64::integer64, hex strings (any case), an h3o H3 vector, or doubles. A double cannot hold a cell exactly (cells are above 2^53), so doubles give a warning of class rcs_warning_h3_double and are then validated like any other input; a cell whose last bits were lost is no longer a valid cell.

Value

A character vector of the same length; NA stays NA. Aborts with class rcs_error_h3_input when a value is not a valid cell or x has another type.

See also

rcs_h3, store_h3_hex() for the cell columns of a data frame.

Examples

cells <- bit64::as.integer64(c("599686042433355775", NA))
rcs_h3_hex(cells)
#> [1] "85283473fffffff" NA               
rcs_h3_hex("85283473FFFFFFF")
#> [1] "85283473fffffff"
rcs_h3_hex(h3o::h3_from_strings("85283473fffffff"))
#> [1] "85283473fffffff"
